answer: Practically, the chain should mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because atlas only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, jade is enforced in the ledger: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any spiral approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
